blocks.prompt: 15. If the arithmetic progressions \(3, 10, 17, \ldots\) and \(63, 65, 67, \ldots\) are such that their \(n^{\text{th}}\) terms are equal, then find the value of \(n\).
blocks.explanation:
Do alag A.P.s hain; kisi ek position \(n\) par dono ki term barabar ho jati hai.
Find kya karna hai? Woh position \(n\).
Plan: dono ki \(n\)th term likhna, barabar rakhna aur \(n\) solve karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: pehli A.P.: \(3, 10, 17, \ldots\); doosri A.P.: \(63, 65, 67, \ldots\)
Humein find karna hai: woh \(n\) jahan dono ki \(n\)th terms barabar hon.
Tareeqa: Dono ke liye \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) likh kar ek linear equation banegi. Dono mein \(n\) ek hi hai kyunke sawal ek hi position ki baat kar raha hai.

Pehli A.P. ki nth term
\[a_1 = 3,\quad d = 7\]
\[a_n = 3 + (n - 1)7 = 7n - 4\]
Kyun: \(10 - 3 = 7\); bracket khola: \(3 + 7n - 7\).

Doosri A.P. ki nth term
\[b_1 = 63,\quad d' = 2\]
\[b_n = 63 + (n - 1)2 = 2n + 61\]
Kyun: \(65 - 63 = 2\); bracket khola: \(63 + 2n - 2\). Doosri A.P. ke liye alag nishan \(b_n\) liya taake dono mix na hon.

Barabar rakh kar solve karein
\[7n - 4 = 2n + 61\]
\[5n = 65\]
\[n = 13\]
Kyun: \(2n\) ko left aur \(-4\) ko right le gaye: \(7n - 2n = 61 + 4\). Pehli A.P. 3 se shuru ho kar har qadam 7 barhti hai, doosri 63 se shuru ho kar sirf 2; is liye pehli A.P. aakhir doosri ko pakar leti hai, aur 13th jagah par dono barabar ho jati hain.
Dhyan dein: Dono A.P.s ka \(d\) alag hai; ek hi \(d\) dono mein laga dena aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[a_{13} = 7(13) - 4 = 87\]
\[b_{13} = 2(13) + 61 = 87 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Dono ki 13th term 87 aayi, to jawab sahi hai.
